payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the background show recognizable basketball-court markings or basketball equipment?
node.criteria: Pass if recognizable court markings or basketball equipment are visible in the background; fail if neither is visible despite an assessable background; unknown if the background cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Look for court markings or basketball equipment in the background as evidence that it is a basketball court. This evidence does not alone establish complete fulfillment.

fulfillment: The binding is too vague and its ellipsis leaves the decision criterion underspecified. Make the node explicitly assess the edited background against the source and requested change, distinguishing a completed recognizable basketball-court setting from partial progress and no progress. The edited image clearly replaces the kitchen with a basketball setting: a hoop, net, and basketballs are visible, though the floor markings are limited. Do not require every feature or treat one support’s contrary description as decisive; inspect the image evidence and reconcile the supports, preserving unknown only when evidence is genuinely insufficient. The repeated disagreement is semantic/evidence interpretation, not a transport or schema failure; confidence variation is a signal to clarify the criterion, not proof the edit is absent.

response.content: {"text":"The node already has a clear, appropriately scoped criterion: recognizable court markings OR basketball equipment, with evidence explicitly not sufficient by itself to establish overall fulfillment. All five traces pass consistently, and the edited image visibly shows a hoop, net, basketballs, and court lines, so there is no demonstrated semantic failure to repair. Preserve this support-level role and avoid adding a requirement to compare source and edit, judge completion versus partial progress, or require every court feature; those are broader fulfillment judgments and could make this check redundant or overly strict. The downstream suggestion that floor markings are limited does not negate the clearly visible basketball equipment. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; retain unknown for genuinely unassessable backgrounds, not merely because markings are incomplete."}
